description: Experience the majestic flavors of Lamb Ouzi, a show-stopping Middle Eastern feast. This recipe guides you through slow roasting a whole lamb cut to tender perfection, infused with aromatic spices. Served traditionally over a bed of fragrant spiced rice, it promises an unforgettable culinary journey for special occasions.

instructions.title: Prepare and Marinate the Lamb
instructions.text: Pat the lamb dry. Score the surface of the lamb shoulder or leg deeply in several places. In a small bowl, combine 1 tbsp Seven Spice, 1/2 tbsp cumin, 1/2 tbsp coriander, 1/2 tsp turmeric, 1/2 tsp cinnamon, 1/4 tsp cardamom, 1 tbsp salt, and 1 tsp black pepper. Rub this spice mixture all over the lamb, ensuring it gets into the scores. Let it marinate at room temperature for at least 30 minutes, or refrigerate for several hours or overnight.

instructions.title: Sear the Lamb
instructions.text: Preheat your oven to 300°F (150°C). In a large, oven-safe Dutch oven or roasting pan over medium-high heat, add 2 tbsp olive oil. Sear the marinated lamb on all sides until beautifully browned and caramelized, about 5-7 minutes per side. This step builds deep flavor.

instructions.title: Slow Roast the Lamb
instructions.text: Remove the lamb from the pan. Add 1 chopped onion and 3 minced garlic cloves to the pan, sauteing until softened, about 5 minutes. Return the lamb to the pan. Pour 2 cups of broth around the lamb. Cover the Dutch oven tightly with its lid or aluminum foil. Transfer to the preheated oven and slow roast for 5-6 hours, or until the lamb is fork-tender and easily pulls away from the bone. Baste occasionally with pan juices.

instructions.title: Prepare the Ouzi Rice
instructions.text: About 45 minutes before the lamb is done, drain the soaked basmati rice. In a large pot, heat 2 tbsp olive oil over medium heat. Add the remaining chopped onion and minced garlic, sauteing until fragrant, about 5 minutes. Stir in the remaining Seven Spice, cumin, coriander, turmeric, cinnamon, and cardamom, along with 1 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp black pepper. Cook for 1 minute until aromatic.

instructions.title: Cook the Rice and Peas
instructions.text: Add the drained basmati rice to the pot with the spices, stirring to coat each grain. Pour in the remaining 4 cups of chicken or lamb broth. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover tightly, and simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until all the liquid is absorbed and the rice is tender. If using, gently stir in the frozen green peas during the last 5 minutes of cooking. Fluff the rice with a fork.

instructions.title: Assemble, Garnish, and Serve
instructions.text: Carefully remove the tender lamb from the Dutch oven and place it on a large serving platter. The meat should be falling off the bone. Arrange the fragrant ouzi rice around the lamb. Drizzle any remaining pan juices over the lamb and rice. Garnish generously with toasted slivered almonds, pine nuts, and fresh chopped parsley or mint. Serve immediately and enjoy this magnificent Middle Eastern feast.

tips: For extra flavor, consider marinating the lamb overnight in the refrigerator. This allows the spices to penetrate deeper into the meat.
Ensure your roasting pan is tightly covered during the slow roasting process to trap steam, which helps tenderize the lamb and keeps it moist.
Serve Lamb Ouzi with a side of refreshing yogurt-cucumber salad or a simple green salad to balance the richness of the dish.
article:
Lamb Ouzi Whole Slow Roasted: The Ultimate Middle Eastern Dinner Recipe

Imagine a dish so grand, so rich in flavor and history, that it's reserved for the most joyous celebrations. That dish is Lamb Ouzi, a magnificent centerpiece of Middle Eastern cuisine, renowned for its incredibly tender, slow-roasted lamb served atop a bed of aromatic spiced rice. If you're looking to impress guests or simply indulge in an unforgettable culinary experience, mastering this Whole Slow Roasted Lamb Ouzi recipe is an absolute must among Middle Eastern dinner recipes. It’s more than just a meal; it’s an event, a tradition, and a testament to the art of slow cooking.

## What is Lamb Ouzi?

Lamb Ouzi (also spelled "Oozie" or "Awzi") is a classic Middle Eastern dish that hails from the Levant and Gulf regions, often gracing tables during holidays, weddings, and special family gatherings. At its heart, Ouzi consists of succulent, fall-off-the-bone lamb—traditionally a whole lamb or a large cut like a leg or shoulder—cooked to perfection and presented over a fragrant pilaf-style rice, typically adorned with toasted nuts and sometimes peas.

The magic of Lamb Ouzi lies in its preparation. The lamb undergoes a long, slow roasting process, allowing its natural flavors to deepen and the meat to become unbelievably tender. This slow cooking method ensures that every bite is moist and melts in your mouth, a stark contrast to quick roasts. The rice, often basmati, is equally important, infused with a symphony of spices like cardamom, cinnamon, and allspice, which complement the richness of the lamb beautifully. It’s a dish that symbolizes hospitality and abundance, a true crown jewel in the repertoire of Middle Eastern dinner recipes.

## Ingredients for Whole Slow Roasted Lamb Ouzi

To create this show-stopping Whole Slow Roasted Lamb Ouzi, you’ll need a selection of high-quality ingredients. The success of the dish hinges on both the quality of your lamb and the freshness of your spices.

For the Lamb:
*   1 whole lamb leg or shoulder (approx. 4-6 kg / 9-13 lbs), bone-in
*   1/4 cup olive oil
*   1/4 cup lemon juice
*   6-8 cloves garlic, minced
*   2 tablespoons sea salt
*   1 tablespoon black pepper
*   1 tablespoon ground cumin
*   1 tablespoon ground coriander
*   1 tablespoon paprika
*   1 teaspoon ground turmeric
*   1 teaspoon ground cinnamon
*   1 teaspoon ground allspice
*   1/2 teaspoon cayenne pepper (optional, for a little heat)
*   1/2 cup plain yogurt (optional, for extra tenderizing)

For the Spiced Rice:
*   4 cups basmati rice
*   2 tablespoons olive oil or ghee
*   1 large onion, finely chopped
*   4 cloves garlic, minced
*   6 whole green cardamom pods
*   2 cinnamon sticks
*   4-5 whole cloves
*   1 bay leaf
*   1 teaspoon ground allspice
*   1/2 teaspoon ground black pepper
*   6 cups chicken or vegetable broth
*   1 cup frozen green peas (optional)
*   Salt to taste

For Garnish:
*   1/2 cup pine nuts, toasted
*   1/2 cup slivered almonds, toasted
*   Fresh parsley, chopped

## Step-by-Step Guide to Making Lamb Ouzi

Making Whole Slow Roasted Lamb Ouzi is a labor of love, but the steps are straightforward and the result is immensely rewarding.

1.  **Prepare the Lamb:**
    *   Rinse the lamb leg or shoulder thoroughly and pat it completely dry with paper towels.
    *   Using a sharp knife, score the surface of the lamb in a diamond pattern, about 1/2 inch deep. This helps the marinade penetrate.
    *   In a small bowl, combine olive oil, lemon juice, minced garlic, salt, black pepper, cumin, coriander, paprika, turmeric, cinnamon, allspice, and cayenne (if using). If using yogurt, mix it in now.
    *   Rub the marinade generously all over the lamb, ensuring it gets into the scores. For best results, place the lamb in a large roasting bag or cover tightly and refrigerate for at least 12 hours, or preferably 24 hours.

2.  **Slow Roast the Lamb:**
    *   Preheat your oven to 150°C (300°F).
    *   Place the marinated lamb in a large, sturdy roasting pan. Add about 1 cup of water or broth to the bottom of the pan to create steam and prevent drying.
    *   Cover the roasting pan tightly with heavy-duty aluminum foil or use an oven-safe roasting bag.
    *   Roast for 6-8 hours, or until the lamb is incredibly tender and easily pulls away from the bone. The exact time will depend on the size of your lamb and your oven. A good indicator of readiness is an internal temperature of around 90-95°C (195-205°F).
    *   During the last hour of cooking, you can remove the foil to allow the exterior to slightly crisp, if desired.
    *   Once cooked, carefully remove the lamb from the oven and let it rest, covered, for at least 30 minutes before serving. This allows the juices to redistribute, ensuring maximum tenderness.

3.  **Prepare the Spiced Rice:**
    *   While the lamb is resting, prepare the rice. Rinse the basmati rice several times until the water runs clear. Soak it in warm water for 20-30 minutes, then drain well.
    *   In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat olive oil or ghee over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and sauté until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes.
    *   Add minced garlic, whole cardamom pods, cinnamon sticks, whole cloves, and bay leaf. Sauté for another minute until fragrant.
    *   Add the drained rice, ground allspice, and black pepper. Stir gently to coat the rice with the spices and oil, toasting it lightly for 2-3 minutes.
    *   Pour in the chicken or vegetable broth and add salt to taste. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover tightly, and simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until all the liquid is absorbed and the rice is tender.
    *   If using, stir in the frozen green peas during the last 5 minutes of cooking.
    *   Remove from heat and let it sit, covered, for 10 minutes, then fluff with a fork.

4.  **Assemble and Serve:**
    *   On a large serving platter, spread the spiced rice evenly.
    *   Carefully transfer the whole slow roasted lamb onto the bed of rice. The meat should be so tender that it might start to fall apart – that’s perfect!
    *   Garnish generously with toasted pine nuts, slivered almonds, and fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately.

## Tips for Perfectly Slow Roasted Lamb

Achieving that perfect, succulent Lamb Ouzi requires a few key considerations:

*   **Marination is Key:** Don't skimp on the marinating time. It's crucial for infusing flavor deep into the meat and contributing to its tenderness.
*   **Low and Slow is the Way:** Resist the urge to crank up the heat. The low oven temperature and extended cooking time are what break down the tough fibers in the lamb, resulting in that coveted melt-in-your-mouth texture.
*   **Keep it Covered:** Covering the roasting pan tightly with foil or using a roasting bag traps moisture, creating a steamy environment that prevents the lamb from drying out.
*   **Resting is Essential:** Just like any large cut of meat, allowing the lamb to rest after roasting redistributes the juices, ensuring a more tender and flavorful result.
*   **Quality Lamb Matters:** Start with good quality lamb from a reputable butcher. The flavor foundation comes from the meat itself.

## Serving Suggestions for Lamb Ouzi

Lamb Ouzi is a feast in itself, but a few simple accompaniments can enhance the dining experience:

*   **Yogurt Sauce:** A simple, refreshing yogurt sauce (laban) with minced garlic and dried mint provides a lovely contrast to the richness of the lamb.
*   **Fresh Salads:** A crisp Middle Eastern salad like Fattoush or Tabbouleh offers a burst of freshness and acidity.
*   **Pickles:** Assorted pickled vegetables are a traditional accompaniment, providing a tangy counterpoint.
*   **Warm Bread:** Fresh pita bread or another flatbread is perfect for scooping up any remaining rice and juices.

## Variations and Substitutions for Ouzi

While this recipe focuses on Whole Slow Roasted Lamb Ouzi, there are several ways to adapt it:

*   **Meat Cuts:** If a whole leg or shoulder is too much, you can use smaller lamb cuts like shanks or even large chunks of boneless lamb shoulder. Adjust cooking times accordingly.
*   **Rice Mix-ins:** Many Ouzi recipes incorporate ground beef or lamb (known as "Hashweh") cooked with the rice, adding another layer of flavor and texture. Green peas and carrots are also common additions to the rice.
*   **Spice Blends:** Feel free to adjust the spice blend to your preference. Some regions might use more black pepper, others might include dried lime (loomi) in the rice.
*   **Stuffing the Lamb:** A more elaborate variation involves partially deboning the lamb leg, stuffing it with the spiced rice mixture, and then roasting it. This is a more advanced technique but yields an incredibly impressive presentation.

## Frequently Asked Questions About Lamb Ouzi

**Q: Can I make Ouzi with smaller cuts of lamb?**
A: Absolutely! While a whole leg or shoulder is traditional for its grandeur, you can certainly use smaller cuts like lamb shanks or even boneless shoulder pieces. Adjust your roasting time accordingly.

**Q: What kind of rice is best for Ouzi?**
A: Basmati rice is highly recommended due to its long, slender grains that cook up fluffy and separate, perfectly absorbing the aromatic spices.

**Q: How long does it take to slow roast a whole lamb leg?**
A: For a 4-6 kg (9-13 lbs) lamb leg, expect to slow roast it for 6-8 hours at 150°C (300°F). The key is to cook until the meat is fork-tender and easily pulls from the bone.

**Q: Can I prepare parts of Ouzi in advance?**
A: Yes, you can marinate the lamb up to 2 days in advance. You can also toast the nuts for garnish ahead of time. The rice is best cooked fresh, but you can have all your spices measured and ready to go.

**Q: What makes Lamb Ouzi special compared to other lamb dishes?**
A: The combination of the incredibly long, slow roasting process that renders the lamb exceptionally tender, paired with the deeply aromatic and spiced rice, elevates Lamb Ouzi to a truly celebratory and uniquely Middle Eastern experience. It's a dish designed to be shared and savored.
